title: failed_logins is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent login requests defeat the 5-attempt lockout and enable large-scale online password guessing against the admin console
category: authentication / race condition (CWE-362 lost update, CWE-307 insufficient attempt limiting)
evidence: auth.go:34 `	if err := s.db.Where("username = ?", req.Username).First(&u).Error; err != nil {` is the only read of the AdminUser row in the request; auth.go:115 `	u.FailedLogins++` performs the increment in Go memory, auth.go:116 `	updates := map[string]any{"failed_logins": u.FailedLogins}` and auth.go:121 `	s.db.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Where("id = ?", u.ID).Updates(updates)` write the whole stale value back. The lockout decision itself is taken from the stale value: auth.go:117 `	if u.FailedLogins >= 5 {`. There is no `gorm.Expr("failed_logins + 1")`, no `s.db.Transaction`, no `clause.Locking`, and no per-user mutex anywhere on this path (repo grep for singleflight|sync.Mutex|TryLock hits only slb.go, metrics.go, runtime/manager.go, audit/hub.go, quota/quota.go — never admin auth). The read/write pair straddles the CPU-bound secret check at auth.go:76 `	if err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(req.Password)); err != nil {` (cost 10 per main.go:175 `	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(pass), bcrypt.DefaultCost)`), so the race window is ~60-100 ms wide and grows with the attacker's own concurrency. Intent and contract: auth.go:113 `// onMFAFail 连续 5 次失败锁定账户（REQ-022 ②）` and prd.md:362 `① 密码验证 → MFA 状态检查 → 跳转 MFA 验证页 ② 验证码错误重试，连续 5 次失败后锁定账户 ③ 支持备用恢复码登录`. The codebase already uses the atomic idiom elsewhere — quota.go:90 `				UpdateColumn("total_hits", gorm.Expr("total_hits + ?", n))` and quota.go:201 `					UpdateColumn("used_value", gorm.Expr("used_value + ?", delta))` — proving the omission is a defect, not a framework limitation.
impact: K parallel wrong-password POSTs to /api/admin/v1/auth/login all read `failed_logins = N` and all write `N+1` (last-writer-wins; with db.go:52 `			sqlDB.SetMaxOpenConns(1)` the K writes serialise and all succeed, and auth.go:121 discards the error), so the counter advances by ~1 per burst instead of K. The hard ceiling of 5 attempts becomes ~5×K guesses per 15-minute lock cycle, and because locked_until merely expires (model.go:29 `	return u.LockedUntil != nil && time.Now().Before(*u.LockedUntil)`) while failed_logins is never reset on expiry, the budget refreshes indefinitely at the attacker's bcrypt-throughput rate. No compensating control exists: routes.go:42 `	api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)` has no middleware at all, main.go's global chain is only SetTrustedProxies(92)/Recovery(95)/security headers(97-103)/access log(106-118), and the quota limiters are API-key scoped (`func (rl *RateLimiter) Allow(snap *runtime.Snapshot, apiKeyID uint, alias string)`, quota.go:55). The default deployment is single-factor despite MFA being 'on' globally (settings.go:87 `	return Security{MFAEnabled: true, MFARequiredAll: false, RecoveryCodeCount: 10, GraceDays: 7}`): the gate is per-user at auth.go:86 `	if sec.MFAEnabled && u.MFAEnabled {` and the bootstrapped admin has no MFA bound (main.go:179 `	u := model.AdminUser{Username: cfg.AdminUser, PasswordHash: string(hash)}`), with forced binding off (auth.go:133 `	needBind := sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled`). A successful guess therefore hands over a full admin JWT (auth.go:110 → issueLogin → auth.Issue) — provider API keys, gateway keys, guard rules, call audit export and DB backups (routes.go:55-148). The same counter also guards the TOTP/recovery-code steps (auth.go:67, auth.go:104), so accounts that did bind MFA are subject to the identical burst amplification against their 6-digit code. Aggravating: clientIP (server.go:108-115) trusts X-Forwarded-For unconditionally, and the IsLocked gate (auth.go:38) is itself evaluated from the stale read, so in-flight requests complete their password comparison even after the lock is written.
mitigations_checked: No SQL-side atomic increment on this path (grep gorm.Expr: only quota.go:90/201 and tokenstats date buckets). No transaction/row lock: auth.go uses no `s.db.Transaction` (only models.go:95/145, providers.go:309, runtime/bundle.go:80 do). No per-user/per-IP lock or singleflight anywhere in internal/admin. `sqlDB.SetMaxOpenConns(1)` (db.go:52) serialises statements, not request logic — GORM commits an implicit autocommit tx per statement and PrepareStmt is off, so the connection is released before bcrypt and the race survives; it also removes any SQLITE_BUSY signal that might otherwise have failed some writes. WAL (db.go:61) and `TranslateError: true` (db.go:45) provide no isolation across the read/write pair. `utcPool`/`utcTx` (db.go:56-60, utcnormalizer.go:61-111) only normalise time.Time bind args and add no locking. The written value is always a valid non-negative int (no overflow/negative path), the lockout threshold 5 is not client-influenced, locked_until is compared with server time so there is no client-side bypass, and successful login resets the counter (auth.go:81-83 `	u.FailedLogins = 0` / `	Update("failed_logins", 0)`) — none of which addresses the lost update. Gateway rate limits (quota.RateLimiter / quota.RedisLimiter) are API-key/model-alias scoped and never applied to admin routes; deploy/ contains no nginx/limit_req throttle for /api/admin/v1/auth/login. TRUSTED_PROXIES is empty by default but that only affects c.ClientIP(), which is used solely for audit logging here. No CORS/mutating-browser path is needed: the endpoint is unauthenticated by design.
exploit_sketch:
Default install (ADMIN_USER=admin per config.go:65, ADMIN_PASSWORD unset → main.go:172 `		pass = "admin123" // 仅在未设置环境变量时默认，首次启动后必须修改`), admin has no MFA bound.

1. Single burst of 200 wrong-password POSTs:
   for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"admin","password":"guess-'$RANDOM'"}' & done; wait
   All 200 read the same row at auth.go:34 (failed_logins = 0), all 200 run bcrypt at auth.go:76, all 200 write failed_logins = 1 (auth.go:116/121); auth.go:117 sees 1 < 5, so no lockout for any of them. Cost to the account: 1 counted attempt. Guesses delivered: 200.

2. Keep requests pipelined (one starts as another finishes) so the persisted counter advances at ~1 per ~60-100 ms while the guess rate is K× that — 16 counted attempts/second vs hundreds of guesses/second.

3. After ~5 counted increments the account locks for 15 minutes (auth.go:118-119 `		loc := time.Now().Add(15 * time.Minute)`); locked_until then expires and failed_logins is left dirty, so the cycle restarts — ~1000+ guesses per cycle, unbounded over time.

4. The guess that matches reaches auth.go:110 `	s.issueLogin(c, &u, sec)` → auth.Issue → full admin session: read provider keys (/api/admin/v1/providers, /apikeys), mint/delete gateway keys, mutate guard rules, export call audit and DB backups.
recommendation: Do the increment in SQL and decide the lockout from the persisted value: `if err := s.db.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Where("id = ?", u.ID).UpdateColumn("failed_logins", gorm.Expr("failed_logins + 1")).Error; err != nil { ... }` then `var n int64; s.db.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Where("id = ?", u.ID).Pluck("failed_logins", &n)` and set `locked_until` only when `n >= 5`; or wrap read+increment+lock in `s.db.Transaction(...)` with `clause.Locking{Strength: "UPDATE"}` for postgres/mysql. Re-read (or re-check) the lock state immediately before issuing a token so in-flight requests cannot complete after a concurrent lock. Better still, move the failure counter into the shared mfaStore (Redis INCR+EXPIRE, or a mutex-guarded in-memory map keyed by username for the single-node SQLite case) so it is atomic and multi-instance-correct. In parallel, add a per-IP + per-username token bucket in front of routes.go:42 (respecting TRUSTED_PROXIES and removing the unconditional X-Forwarded-For trust in server.go:108-115), reset failed_logins when locked_until lapses, and audit/alert on lock events. Apply the same fix to recovery_codes_json consumption (auth.go:60-63, auth.go:97-101) — see authn-9.
reason: CONFIRMED with exact, verbatim citations and an unbroken chain; severity high is correct. Every quoted line was re-read in place: auth.go:34 (sole row read), auth.go:115 `u.FailedLogins++` (the reported line is the mutation, so the line number is right; 121 is only the write), auth.go:116-121 (whole-value write-back), auth.go:117 (lockout decision taken from the stale Go-side value), auth.go:81-83 (reset), auth.go:113 (REQ-022 ② intent), model.go:29 (server-time lock compare), db.go:45/52/61 (TranslateError, SetMaxOpenConns(1), WAL). The race is not theoretical: the window between read and write contains bcrypt cost-10 (main.go:175) and settings.LoadKV (auth.go:43), i.e. ~60-100 ms per request, and it is widened by the attacker's own concurrency, which is the entire point of the amplification. SQLite provides no refuge — the single connection serialises statements but the implicit per-statement transaction is committed and the connection released long before auth.go:76, so all K writes succeed and clobber each other; the discarded error at auth.go:121 means even a write failure would be silent. No locking idiom exists on this path anywhere in internal/admin (grep for Transaction/gorm.Expr/singleflight/sync.Mutex/TryLock), while the safe atomic idiom is demonstrably available in the same repo (quota.go:90, quota.go:201), so this is a genuine defect rather than a limitation of GORM or SQLite. Privilege assumptions hold: the endpoint is unauthenticated (routes.go:42, no middleware in main.go's chain), the inputs are attacker-controlled JSON (auth.go:29), the target username is public (config.go:65, main.go:179), and there is no per-IP or per-route throttle (the quota limiters are API-key scoped, quota.go:55; deploy/ has no proxy throttle). MFA does not rescue the default deployment because the gate is per-user (auth.go:86) and the bootstrapped admin has no secret bound (main.go:179) with forcing disabled (auth.go:133) — so a correct guess is direct admin-console account takeover, matching the 'high = ... or account takeover' rubric. Refinements recorded for accuracy, none severity-changing: 'essentially unbounded' overstates it slightly — the persisted counter does advance ~1 per non-overlapping burst, so the practical budget is ~5×K guesses per 15-minute cycle, and because failed_logins is never reset when locked_until lapses (a separate finding, authn-1) that budget refreshes indefinitely; the auth.go:38 IsLocked gate is also evaluated from the same stale read, so already-in-flight requests finish their password comparison after the lock lands; and the auth.go:81-83 reset races with concurrent stale failure writes, so a burst containing the correct password can have its reset clobbered. The finding's parenthetical that the identical pattern breaks recovery-code single-use (auth.go:60-63 / 97-101 write back a JSON list derived from the auth.go:34 row) is likewise supported by the code and is correctly deferred to authn-9. Kept at high rather than critical because it yields takeover only if the password is inside the attacker's dictionary and grants no direct code execution or authz bypass; kept above medium because the broken control is the PRD-mandated primary brute-force defence (prd.md:362), not defense-in-depth. Defaults (JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY) contribute nothing new here, and none of the pre-agreed architecture caveats (WriteTimeout=0, TRUSTED_PROXIES, faithful passthrough, no CORS) were counted as mitigations or as this finding's impact.
